queries.query: the claim that Adam already possessed every art, and that this knowledge, carved in stone against the coming flood, descended through the Chaldeans and Egyptians to Hermes Trismegistus
queries.note: Ch. I-II on the origin of the philosophers' stone; 'first inventor of arts', 'hieroglyphical characters', 'king, priest, prophet, magician, sophist' paraphrased away; Adam and Hermes Trismegistus kept as reader-honest names.

queries.query: a catalogue of failed seekers of the stone: those who hunted it in plant juices, those who tried animal matter and blood, and the frauds whose counterfeit metal ruined goldsmiths and coiners
queries.note: The chapters against sophists seeking the stone in vegetables and animals; 'Lac Virginis', 'fixatory waters', 'mint-masters', and the named targets (Geber, Rupescissa) paraphrased away.

queries.query: why the stone requires a marriage of Sol and Luna, husband and wife who cannot generate anything without a third animated seed from them both
queries.note: The two matters of the Stone; 'proper marriage, both natural and artificial', 'seed and sperm of both' paraphrased; Sol and Luna kept as the alchemical names every reader of the literature knows.

queries.query: where did the most ancient wisdom come from and how was it handed down
queries.note: The Chaldean-Egyptian-Greek transmission chain; primordial-wisdom lineages are claimed by many traditions. No target — graded post-hoc.

queries.query: what is man made of, and what makes him a small mirror of the whole creation
queries.note: Man as quintessence extracted from elements and stars; microcosm doctrine is answered across many traditions. No target — graded post-hoc.
